pr.title: Feature flag: rolling-updates

raw_findings.body: The unqualified name FEATURE_DISABLED can be mistaken for a boolean flag rather than an exit-code value, reducing readability and increasing the chance of misuse when the interface is extended further.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Naming convention silently violated, reducing maintainability and readability of the shared exit-code contract.
raw_findings.impact: The unqualified name FEATURE_DISABLED can be mistaken for a boolean flag rather than an exit-code value, reducing readability and increasing the chance of misuse when the interface is extended further.
raw_findings.root_cause: New exit-code constant was added without following the existing _EXIT_CODE suffix convention used by sibling constants in the same interface.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the constant to FEATURE_DISABLED_EXIT_CODE to match the ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE / RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE naming convention used in the same interface.
raw_findings.title: FEATURE_DISABLED exit-code constant breaks the established naming convention
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads the interface next to ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and needs to identify which constants represent CLI exit codes.

raw_findings.body: A regression in this new gating branch (wrong exit code, missing message, or accidental fallthrough into validateConfig()) would not be caught by any automated test.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regression of the feature-gating logic can pass CI undetected.
raw_findings.impact: A regression in this new gating branch (wrong exit code, missing message, or accidental fallthrough into validateConfig()) would not be caught by any automated test.
raw_findings.root_cause: New conditional branch was introduced without an accompanying test verifying its behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit/CLI test that invokes UpdateCompatibilityCheck with ROLLING_UPDATES disabled and asserts the feature-disabled message is printed and exit code CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED is returned.
raw_findings.title: New feature-disabled exit path in UpdateCompatibilityCheck has no test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Running `kc.sh update-compatibility check` while the rolling-updates preview feature is disabled (the default state).

raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regression of the feature-gating logic can pass CI undetected.
raw_findings.impact: A regression in this new gating branch (wrong exit code, missing message, or accidental fallthrough into validateConfig()/writeToFile()) would not be caught by any automated test.
raw_findings.root_cause: New conditional branch was introduced without an accompanying test verifying its behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit/CLI test that invokes UpdateCompatibilityMetadata with ROLLING_UPDATES disabled and asserts the feature-disabled message is printed and exit code CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED is returned, and that no metadata file is written.
raw_findings.title: New feature-disabled exit path in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata has no test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Running `kc.sh update-compatibility metadata` while the rolling-updates preview feature is disabled (the default state).

raw_findings.body: Because the identical 5-line block is copy-pasted into both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of being placed in the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand base class (which already hosts printPreviewWarning/printFeatureDisabled), the two commands can drift out of sync if only one copy is updated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Code duplication increases maintenance risk of inconsistent feature-gating behavior between related commands.
raw_findings.impact: Because the identical 5-line block is copy-pasted into both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of being placed in the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand base class (which already hosts printPreviewWarning/printFeatureDisabled), the two commands can drift out of sync if only one copy is updated.
raw_findings.root_cause: Identical conditional block was duplicated into two sibling command classes instead of being centralized in the shared abstract base class.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Factor the feature-enabled check into a shared method (e.g., `boolean checkRollingUpdatesEnabledOrExit()`) in AbstractUpdatesCommand and call it from both run() implementations.
raw_findings.title: Feature-enabled check duplicated between UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata
raw_findings.trigger: A future change to the ROLLING_UPDATES gating logic (e.g., message text, exit code, or feature key) needs to be applied consistently to both the `check` and `metadata` subcommands.

finding.body: The unqualified name FEATURE_DISABLED can be mistaken for a boolean flag rather than an exit-code value, reducing readability and increasing the chance of misuse when the interface is extended further.
finding.failure_mode: Naming convention silently violated, reducing maintainability and readability of the shared exit-code contract.
finding.impact: The unqualified name FEATURE_DISABLED can be mistaken for a boolean flag rather than an exit-code value, reducing readability and increasing the chance of misuse when the interface is extended further.
finding.root_cause: New exit-code constant was added without following the existing _EXIT_CODE suffix convention used by sibling constants in the same interface.

finding.title: FEATURE_DISABLED exit-code constant breaks the established naming convention
finding.trigger: A developer reads the interface next to ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and needs to identify which constants represent CLI exit codes.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that FEATURE_DISABLED breaks a naming convention is incorrect. Looking at the interface, ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE use _EXIT_CODE suffix, but these are specifically for upgrade result codes. FEATURE_DISABLED represents a different semantic category (feature state, not upgrade result), so the naming is intentionally different. This is a stylistic opinion without concrete defect.

finding.body: Because the identical 5-line block is copy-pasted into both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of being placed in the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand base class (which already hosts printPreviewWarning/printFeatureDisabled), the two commands can drift out of sync if only one copy is updated.

finding.suggested_fix: Factor the feature-enabled check into a shared method (e.g., `boolean checkRollingUpdatesEnabledOrExit()`) in AbstractUpdatesCommand and call it from both run() implementations.
